entries.en: No, sir. Just pointing out our peculiar legal situation. You're welcome to look around, but this can't be considered a formal inspection.
This ship is Council property right now. So, respectfully, please clear the gangway.
Normandy is not legally part of the Alliance Military. I can't allow you aboard without permission from the Office of Special Tactics and Reconnaissance.
I'm sure you'll find everything in order, Admiral.
This is a surprise.
[Salute]
Think of it as an opportunity.
I don't like it either.
I had orders.
She's not overdesigned.
Don't insult my ship!
Please do.
You can look around.
Damn right I did.
I'm afraid so.
Commander, I suggest you secure your mouth. It's going to get you in trouble.
I'll be submitting a report to the Joint Military Council. It will not be as negative as I had planned.
Good hunting, Commander Shepard. Make us proud.
Your opinions have some merit, Commander. I'll take them into consideration when I write my report to the Joint Military Command.
I'll be sending my report and corrective recommendations to the Joint Military Command.
Not that I expect them to do anything about it. Too many interest groups have too much money invested in this.
Who designed that CIC? Putting the commander aft of everyone else is inefficient. What if he needs to discuss with the operators toward the bow?
Hm. Reasonable goal. But they should have studied that in a lab rather than on a front-line warship.
A fair point. I suppose the design has no chance of becoming standard. No need to worry about a generation of recruits learning things bass-ackwards.
Which only works so long as you all have working radios. Maybe your DC drills should include sign language.
I had to shake my head at that drive core of yours. 120 billion credits of element zero to make this thing able to move without giving itself away.
You realize we could make drive cores for 12,000 fighters with that money? What good is it to hide for a few hours, anyway? Useless!
Maybe, maybe. But that's not the job of a proper warship.
We're supposed to find and kill the enemy fleet, not count how many times their garrison goes to the bathroom.
There's two ways I could take that, Commander. But that is true. I suppose the early U-Boats weren't much better.
Eden Prime does have a smoking crater on it, Commander. Don't break your arm patting yourself on the back.
And we need to talk about your crew, Commander.
Krogan?
Asari?
Turians?
What are you thinking, Commander? You can't allow alien nationals free access to Alliance equipment!
That assumes the hearts and minds are worth winning. That hasn't been proven yet.
Sophistry, Commander. You know I'm right. You want them on board that bad, fine. Don't quote regs at me.
The Council expects a whole hell of a lot from the Alliance, Commander. They better start giving back real damned soon.
You have anything else to say, Commander? Any other justifications for the state of this vessel?
Your job is to look good, Commander. The Alliance Navy's is to win wars.
That assumes Normandy's technologies can become practical in the future.
I'm not convinced Normandy isn't a waste of taxpayer money. But I am convinced that you believe otherwise. And that you'll use it to its best ability.
I don't agree with any of this, but your reasons seem... sound.
I'm sorry to hear that, sir.
Sounds like a fairly common situation.
The simple fact is, I'm also part of the Council's chain of command now. They expect a joint effort. I'm providing one.
I think Normandy is a good ship, sir. Even if you disagree, you have to see that her joint construction and multiracial crew make the Alliance look better.
We showed the Council something they hadn't thought of with our fighter carriers. You may disapprove of Normandy, but she's just another way we're outthinking them.
None, sir.
What did you find out of order?
Modified turian style. They prefer commanders looking over their subordinates, rather than in the middle of them. We wanted to see how effectively they can command with that setup.
There are no amateurs on this crew. They know to keep idle chatter minimized during combat. And I can bellow with the best DIs.
We use our suit or uniform radios. Anyone who needs to talk to me keys in to my line. It's as if they're next to me.
We can loiter in an enemy system and monitor traffic, or drop infiltration teams on enemy worlds. Normandy can be more effective than the salarian STG.
Men of limited vision said the same thing about early aircraft, submarines, and tanks.
It also makes us the fastest ship in the fleet. Without the Tantalus core, Eden Prime would be a smoking crater right now.
Between Saren and the geth, we have enough enemies out here. Treating other species with suspicion and distrust won't win hearts and minds.
I'm Normandy's commanding officer. The regs say I have the authority to say who does and doesn't come aboard. If you disagree, send a complaint up the chain of command.
I bet.
About what?
It's a turian design.
We're trained for it.
Personal radios.
It's useful.
Do you read history?
We're fast, too.
They're allies.
That's my choice to make.
Not my call.
We need to build bridges.
We need to kick ass.
No, Commander. That's something that you get right the first time.
A proactive captain would try.
Do you now? Well, I'll just have a bed made up in your cabin. Camp out until you find a fight. Hm?
I'm so pleased you can wash your hands of it.
I agree, sir. But I don't see what my crew can do about it. That's something you fix in drydock.
You don't expect me to rip out the CIC and redesign it, do you?
Normandy was an expensive ship, sir.
I think you should see her in action before you make that call.
I'm sorry you disapprove, sir.
I was told to make nice with the Council. If that means our military secrets get out, the brass only has themselves to blame.
We can't fix that.
It is a lot of money.
Give it a chance.
You assume I have a choice.
We'll be taking her for counseling.
I wanted to save her. Stupid, huh? I mean, she was just a transport detail. But to see her so...
Right, uh,  you've got things to do. And I've got to collect her.
She's still back there, Commander.
Commander. Glad to see you.
Yes ma'am.
Yes sir.
Behind those shipping containers. I've got a sniper positioned, but I don't think we'll need him. She's only a danger to herself.
We've got a sedative to calm her down, but we can't get close to her. Every step we take gets her more wound up.
I-- I'm just doing my job, Commander.
Thank you again for the help.
I'll-- We'll take good care of her.
Is she all right?
Is it over, Commander?
I appreciate the help. But don't look down on her. She spent the last 13 years getting treated like an animal.
I'll take care of it from here. Commander.
Thanks, Commander. That means a lot. I didn't want to hurt her.
It's just, when I see her curled into a ball, shivering...
She was only six when they took her. Why the hell are we out here if we can't even keep one little girl safe?
Yes ma'am!
Yes sir!
So we clean up the wreckage, shoot the guilty, and hope everyone else learns not to mess with us. Great.
Will that ever be enough?
Thanks for your help, Commander. We are taking her to a counseling center. They'll help her get better.
I should have done something more.
I wish we could have saved her.
I-- I really didn't want to do that.
Please go, Commander.
She deserved a real life.
She's gone?
Yeah. Stupid question.
No. No, I understand.
I had to jump her to get the sedative in. I didn't see any other way.
Wish it were under better circumstances. Where is she?
Just tell me where she is, Lieutenant.
She's back there?
I hope I don't need it. Tell your men to stand by.
You seem awfully worried about her.
One way or another, she's coming out of there.
I'll talk to her. Keep back.
I'm fine. Thanks for asking. I got the sedative in her. She's out.
I just had to jump her to get the sedative in.
She took the sedative. She wants to get better, Lieutenant.
I got her to take her medicine. What a waste of my time.
I got her to take the sedative.
Bad things happen to good people, Lieutenant. That's why you and I are here. Don't wring your hands over her -- help her.
To make people who do these things pay. It's not the severity of punishment that deters crime, it's the certainty.
I don't have any answers for you, Lieutenant. We're doing what we can.
I'm sorry, Lieutenant. I couldn't save her.
You heard the gunshot, and I'm still standing here.
"Is she all right?"
She's fine.
She's down.
It's over.
Don't lose heart.
To get the bastards.
Unfortunately.
I had to help.
Skip the pleasantries.
I'll take care of her.
Your concern
What's the situation, Commander?
I-- I don't think that's necessary, Commander. She's clearly no danger to anyone but herself.
But-- Aye, aye, Commander. I'll take care of her.
